<review_context>
This is a synthetic review, invented to exercise the meltiro engine. It concerns routine durability gauges applied to load-bearing widgets during manufacture and service. Operators record standardised gauge scores at inspection, and cost analysts use those scores for three purposes: costing maintenance programmes; measuring outcomes in whole-life cost appraisals; and estimating transitions between the failure states used in reliability models. The purpose of this review is to assess how well routine gauge scores measure the variables those analysts care about: maintenance cost and resource use; expected service life; and transition between failure states. The gauges in scope are listed below. The aim is to identify every published statistical relationship between a gauge score and a lifecycle outcome, and to assess the strength of those relationships across the published evidence.
